missed.fact: Claim 2 nuance: the receiver anchors on stored dueAt, but the result is the first occurrence strictly after NOW, not one step on. For EveryInterval the grid stays anchored to dueAt (from + k*interval). For Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Weekdays/RandomDays it steps from the previous due and loops until after now. Acknowledging (setDone) does not re-anchor to the ack time. It calls the same nextOccurrenceAfter(current.dueAt, ...) and only when dueAt is already past now. A reminder acknowledged early keeps its dueAt.

Claim 4: the domain type has no minimum. EveryInterval(Duration) is unvalidated at construction, and a zero or negative interval returns null (never repeats). Sub-millisecond intervals also return null. The 5-minute minimum and the 365-day maximum are only UI/quick-add policy (INTERVAL_MIN/INTERVAL_MAX), so synced or stored data below 5 minutes would still schedule.

Claim 5 correction: the gap is NOT stored. It is recomputed on every call from a deterministic seed (occurrence epoch-second, minDays, maxDays), so the same occurrence always yields the same gap. Only the range is persisted, packed as minDays*1000+maxDays. RandomDays requires minDays>=1, maxDays>=minDays and maxDays<=365. The draw is uniform over nextInt(min, max+1), and Random(seed) is fixed by Kotlin's algorithm, so a merge on another platform must reproduce the seed formula exactly to agree.

Claim 6: there is no explicit clamp code. Clamping comes from java.time LocalDateTime.plusMonths, which clamps to the last valid day. Because each step is from the previous occurrence, the day drifts. A reminder on Jan 31 goes to Feb 28, then Mar 28, and does not return to the 31st. The drift is untested by the map.

One column (repeatIntervalMillis) carries three meanings: EVERY_INTERVAL millis, WEEKDAYS bitmask, RANDOM_DAYS packed minDays*1000+maxDays. It is nullable for None/Daily/Weekly/Monthly. The repeatRuleKind column stores string tags (EVERY_INTERVAL, WEEKDAYS, RANDOM_DAYS and the others). The same encoding is duplicated in SyncCodec, so a merge must decode by kind.
The Room mapper errors (error(...)) on a null interval for EVERY_INTERVAL/WEEKDAYS/RANDOM_DAYS, so a merge producing kind without value would crash on read.

Identity and deletion columns on the reminder: primary key id; soft delete via deletedAtMillis; two independent LWW groups (scheduleUpdatedAtMillis/ByDevice covering dueAt and repeat fields, statusUpdatedAtMillis/ByDevice covering done/notified). The repeat rule belongs to the schedule group, and the receiver's roll-forward rewrites dueAt and bumps scheduleUpdatedAt, so a device firing an alarm can win the merge against an edit.

Other repeat-adjacent fields in the same entity: kind (NOTIFICATION/ALARM), nagEnabled/nagMaxRepeats/nagMaxDurationMillis (NagPolicy defaults 3 repeats, 1h), soundRef, done, notified. dueAt is wall-clock LocalDateTime text (dueAtIso), not an instant.

Weekdays alignment: alignToRule moves a dueAt that is not on a selected day forward to the first selected day at the same time, so the stored first occurrence can differ from the chosen date. Only Weekdays does this.

DST handling: nextFireInstant resolves wall-clock to an instant, trying both offsets in a fall-back overlap, and gives a 60-second grace for just-past alarms before rolling forward. Catch-up is capped at 20,000 steps (returns null, i.e. no alarm, beyond that).
